correctness.rationale: For x(t)=x0+vt the full hereditary equation reduces exactly to (1−ρ)v=κvF(|v|), F(r)=∫s w(s)e^(−r²s²/2)ds. F decreases strictly and continuously from 1 to 0 by positivity and dominated convergence, giving a unique nonzero positive speed precisely κ>κc=1−ρ. Monotone convergence applied to (1−F(r))/r² yields M3/2 in extended real numbers; since 1−F(r(κ))=(κ−κc)/κ, lim r²/(κ−κc)=2/(κc M3) (0 for infinite M3). For normalized w_p=(p−1)(p−2)(1+s)^(−p), p>2, verify beta integral normalization, u=rs dominated-convergence Gamma constant C_p for 2<p<4, cutoff Δ4(r)=3r²log(1/r)+O(r²), and M3=6/((p−3)(p−4)) for p>4. Inverting gives the three stated laws, including at p=4 sqrt(2δ/(3κc log(1/δ))). Independent quadrature at r=.001: p3 Δ=.002486726116 vs leading .00250662827; p4 Δ=1.690713762e−5 vs leading 2.072326584e−5; p5 Δ=1.495035001e−6 vs 1.5e−6. The infinite theorem follows from limit arguments, not finite quadratures.
